content: The Consolidated HIV Strategic Information Guidelines: Driving Impact Through Programme Monitoring and Management is a publication by the World Health Organization (WHO) that provides a comprehensive framework for monitoring and evaluating HIV-related programs. The document includes a Web Annex B, which focuses on aligning indicators across global monitoring and evaluation frameworks. This publication is part of the WHO guideline entitled Consolidated HIV Strategic Information Guidelines: Driving Impact Through Programme Monitoring and Management. It is made publicly available for transparency and informational purposes, in accordance with the WHO Handbook for Guideline Development, 2nd edition (2014). Web Annex B specifically addresses the alignment of indicators across global monitoring and evaluation frameworks. Indicators are categorized as follows: Consistent (C), where numerator and denominator definitions are identical; Similar (S), where basic definitions are the same but there are differences in how the numerator or denominator is calculated; and Related (R), where an indicator is reflected only as a numerator, denominator, or disaggregation category in other frameworks. Blank cells indicate that there is no equivalent indicator included in the respective monitoring and evaluation framework. For example, syphilis screening coverage in antenatal care (ANC) is categorized as Consistent (C), while AIDS mortality is also categorized as Consistent (C). The Global Fund for AIDS, TB, and Malaria Modular Framework indicators (version 4 FY20) are referenced in this alignment.
